slides.title: Libraries can be bootstrapped: an 8B wrote MRCR's library.
slides.notes: The chain now runs without hand-written code for a new family: proposer writes, verification accepts, a 0.6B caller trained on other families calls it. Stress the caveat: MRCR is a parsing task in disguise, so this is program discovery. The ladder: the 8B and a 4-bit 14B, both thinking, each succeed on 2 of 5 seeds; scale does not make discovery reliable, though the 14B succeeds sooner when it does. Every trained 4B fails.

slides.title: Discovery on 37 generated families: thinking, scale, and training.
slides.notes: Generated families give resolution MRCR cannot: 37 held-out families per proposer. Thinking and scale both matter. SFT on the 8B's verified code plus 40 steps of RL with the verified teaching score as reward lifts a 4B from 9 to 30 of 74 (replicated). The caution of the day: round four's 42, level with the 8B, was the best of four RL seeds of the same recipe (22, 29, 33, 42). With three times the helper-family teacher data the recipe averages 33.7 over three seeds (32 to 36), matches round four on solves, and reaches the 8B on helper families. Recipe comparisons need several seeds; checkpoints should be chosen on held-out discovery. MRCR still fails.

slides.title: Bootstrapping is cheap where answers are exact (pre-registered).
slides.notes: Two pre-registered tests. E39 on 30 families with two seeds: the trained 4B with eight samples and three labels lands near the thinking 8B with thirty labels (26 vs 29 pooled). E58 is the powered follow-up on 141 untouched families: 75 vs 73; it met the registered 10-point non-inferiority margin with families as the unit, but not with the 37 templates as the unit, and only for the chosen (best) checkpoint; the weakest checkpoint scores 67 vs 73. The price is false acceptance: 10 of 85 accepted libraries are wrong (all six semantic totals; three day spans that subtract timestamps instead of dates), against none for the labelled protocol. Combined proposer tokens are about a third of the 8B's. Mechanism: on exact families, reproducing three examples and running cleanly is nearly sufficient.

slides.title: Libraries generalize in length, not in wording; the harness can fix that.
slides.notes: New on 24 October. Frozen libraries survive five-times-longer inputs (55 of 55) but not a reworded question (3 of 55) or even 'QUESTION:' changed to 'Q:'. Teaching on varied wordings or telling the proposer did not fix it. A 4B reading only the question returns the family's parameters 96 percent of the time on unseen rewordings; wrapping the same frozen libraries in that parser repairs 54 of 55. But a 4B proposer told to write such an interface almost never does (1 of 11, 0 of 18), and editing a working library gets 3 of 12. Executors generalize; small proposers do not write robust interfaces: acquisition is the open problem. Caveat: the wrapper is the known semantic-parser-plus-executor pattern, hand-written here with the family's template.

slides.title: One line of documentation decides whether an untrained caller uses a library.
slides.notes: The cleanest result of the day. Same code, four docstrings. The usage line alone carries the effect. The practical rule: every library ships with a usage line; the bootstrapper now inserts one. The deeper point: an untrained caller reads documentation, a distilled caller has learned the call.

slides.title: MuSiQue in long haystacks: capacity belongs in choosing evidence.
slides.notes: MuSiQue is where the routine needs helper calls. The two-round library wins on accuracy and cost through the 0.6B caller. Everything that adds capacity elsewhere (recursion, bigger reader, more samples) does not help. The gap to gold paragraphs (about 0.2) is evidence selection.

slides.title: External validity, and what we withdrew.
slides.notes: LongBench-v2 is the external-validity check. The first generic library (map-reduce notes) tied direct reading at nine times the cost; a retrieval library (BM25 over passages for the question and each option, one read) beats direct reading on all 503 questions, 0.427 against 0.356 (+0.07, se 0.02), at a quarter of its tokens, also through the 0.6B caller; the first 150-question sample had suggested +0.11. The lesson matches MuSiQue: choose evidence, do not summarize everything. Two earlier readings were withdrawn after fresh samples. The method lessons are the ones that cost most: scripted harnesses that did not match the kernel, verification sets that did not span deployment lengths.

slides.title: What this changes, and what to test next.
slides.notes: The thesis moved today. A skeptical review (Codex, as a committee member) listed prior art for almost every mechanism; the defensible contribution is measured on small models: acquiring robust procedures cheaply, and where it breaks. Item 1 decides the framing: if a tool loop ties the REPL and acquired routines hold up and amortize, the thesis is about acquisition; if plain tools match the library, the distinctive claim is gone. Ask the advisor whether that framing is the right one.
